chapter.title: The Mission Room
chapter.sub: A record crest by eight. Every system under stress at once — including the engineer.
chapter.status: **DRAFT** · scripted from the series plan · IDs provisional

items.text: SEASON 11 · EPISODE 10 · DRAFT · SEASON FINALE  The Brennock County EOC · the night before the record crest · Maya, Director Oduya, Kit, and every owner in the room · Level L6 · Mastery support (reference only — choose the tool and say why)  The Sable River is going to a record crest by eight tomorrow. Everything this season fixed is about to be tested at once — and so is the person who fixed it.  ⚑ RV-182: every system and every decision has an owner. RV-184: warnings verbatim; evacuations are the director's. RV-185: fatigue is a risk the roster manages. MD-01 / MD-02: the season boss. Some choices run on a clock — and some depend on your loadout.

items.title: The Mission Room
items.stakes: A record crest by eight. Carrier A down, a dam rumour, a warning on its way — and the principal engineer at hour fifteen.
items.reward: A room that holds every critical service, every word in its owner's voice — and an engineer who hands over and sleeps.

objectives.text: Decide what the application stands on

items.rumor: Everything this season built, at once — including the handover.

items.text: Cold open — “Tell me what we can trust”

items.alt: The EOC at night, every desk staffed, the video wall full of river gauges; Director Oduya points at the wall; Maya has just walked in, coat still on.

bubbles.text: Record crest by eight. Tell me what we can trust.
B, the gateway, the stream and the relay. And I'm at hour fifteen.

items.caption: Every part of the room, under stress at once.

lines.text: Record crest by eight. Tell me what we can trust.
B, the gateway, the stream and the relay. And one more thing: I'm at hour fifteen.

items.prompt: 22:12. You've just walked in. The director wants to know what she can trust. Your first minute?
items.happening: Record crest by 08:00; carrier A down; you just walked in.
items.risk: A director deciding blind — and an engineer at hour fifteen deciding alone.
timeout: She asks Wendell, Fitz and Hektor one at a time, and loses ten minutes.

hints.text: What does the director need to know — about the room, and about you?

options.label: Get on the router and force traffic back to carrier A the moment it answers
options.result: Wendell, across the room: “Failback's manual during an activation. That's the whole point.”
options.consequence: Touches someone else's network — and undoes a fix.
options.fail: The network is Wendell's, and failback during an activation is manual by design.

options.label: Facts for the director: carrier B carrying, pinned; the gateway, the stream and the relay up; A down; the generator not load-tested this month — and that you're at hour fifteen, so Kit's brief starts now
options.result: Oduya: “Good. Then the next thing I want is that brief in your hand.”
options.consequence: Facts to the person who decides — including the fact about you.

options.label: Tell her everything's fine — she has enough to worry about
Go straight to the radio room — the gateway is the thing only you really know
options.result: The director asks again, louder. And nobody starts the brief.
options.consequence: That's the sentence from hour sixteen.

items.title: One bridge, again.
items.body: Wendell pulls the river gauge at the Mill Road bridge onto the status board: 0.15 m below the deck at 22:20, rising 0.30 m an hour. Carrier B — the one carrying everything tonight — crosses the Sable in the same conduit as A, hung under that deck. The separate hilltop path the tranche paid for came into service two weeks ago; nothing has needed it yet. t = d ÷ v: half an hour. 22:50.
items.label: Test: when the water's on the deck — and why B goes with A.

items.alt: A chart of the river level at the Mill Road bridge against the deck from 22:00 to 23:30. A solid gauge line rises from 0.25 m below the deck to 0.15 m below at 22:20; a dashed line at the same rate crosses the deck at 22:50 and reaches 0.20 m above by 23:30. Both carriers' conduit hangs beneath the deck.
items.caption: Half an hour.

items.title: ‘crossing: Mill Road bridge · under-deck conduit’
items.body: Carrier B's route map, the page Wendell found in Episode 2: ‘Crossing: Mill Road bridge, under-deck conduit, shared.’ Tonight it has a time next to it, in Wendell's pencil: 22:50.

items.sub: Mastery · the skill behind this chapter

items.alt: A teaching moment: Oduya and Maya beside a board. Record crest by eight. Carrier A is down, a rumour says the dam's gone, and you're at hour fifteen. Then the first thing I do is tell you what we can trust. The second is write Kit's brief. Good. The third is go home when he's here.

Which do you calculate first — the room's power margin, or the time a proper handover needs — and why?   Which relationship do you reach for?  Payback time  Rate  Time budget     Reference: the 📖 Glossary has every formula. At mastery, knowing  which  and  why  is the skill.

items.prompt: 22:21. Water on the bridge deck by 22:50; carrier B crosses in the same conduit as A. What do you ask for?
items.risk: Everything that leaves the room, gone at once.
timeout: At 22:50 the room loses the outside world for four minutes while Wendell scrambles.

hints.text: Which path doesn't cross the river?

items.note: Draft decision (DR-S11E10). Option B needs Redundancy at LIMITED or better.

options.label: Trust B — it's carried everything all night
options.result: At 22:50 the water's on the deck and B goes with it: the stream, the relay and the partners, all at once.
options.consequence: Hopes the shared path isn't shared.

options.label: Ask Wendell to bring the hilltop microwave path into service now — his routing, Fitz's radio; nobody goes near the tower or the bridge
options.result: At 22:37 the hilltop path carries a share of everything. At 22:50 carrier B drops, and nothing on the floor notices.
options.consequence: Use the separate path before the shared one fails — through its owners.

options.label: Ask Wendell to bring up the bonded-cellular kit for the stream and the alert relay
options.result: The stream and the warnings stay up at a lower bitrate. At 22:50 the partner bridge — the state and the dam operator — goes dark.
options.consequence: The best you can do without the separate path: what's mission-critical, not everything.

options.label: Send public works to check the conduit under the bridge
options.result: Nobody goes onto a flooding bridge at night — for a cable.
options.consequence: Puts people where the water is.
options.fail: Nobody goes onto a flooding bridge for a cable.

items.title: The warnings nobody believed
items.body: On 31 May 1889, after days of heavy rain, the South Fork Dam above Johnstown, Pennsylvania, failed, and a wall of water swept through the town below; more than 2,200 people died. Telegraph warnings about the dam had reached the town that day — but there had been warnings about that dam in earlier years, and nothing had happened, so many people did not act. A warning is only as strong as the trust behind it. Relaying rumours as warnings, or rewriting real warnings to sound calmer, spends that trust.

items.title: Hour fifteen.
items.body: The roster board by the status wall carries the rule Maya asked the director to enforce: twelve on, ten off. Under ENGINEERING it says MAYA · ON 07:00 — the rebuild application all day at the county offices, then the call. At 22:00 she passed hour fifteen: 15 ÷ 12 = 125% of her roster. Hour sixteen — the hour she patched the wrong talkgroup — is 23:00. Kit is rostered on at 23:00 and on his way in early. The brief isn't written.
items.label: Test: the hours — and the share of the roster.

items.alt: The engineering roster for the 12th as a timeline from 06:00 to midnight: Maya on since 07:00, her bar grey to hour 12 at 19:00 and red after it, with hour 16 marked at 23:00; Fitz 11:00 to 23:00; Quino from 19:00 to 07:00; Kit rostered from 23:00. A NOW line at 22:30.
items.caption: The roster counts her too.

items.alt: Maya in the EOC at night in red alarm light, the wall's picture frozen behind her. Stamped over the scene: dam?, PW-FLOOD-2, 96%, hour 16.
narration: Everything above happened one call at a time. On the night before the crest it didn't. From 22:30 to 23:30 every pressure touched every other one — including the clock on Maya.
items.caption: Take the engineering desk. Hand it over well.

items.label: **☢ Meltdown:** the mission room, all at once — paths, words, power, radios, a rumour, a laptop, and hour sixteen. Almost nothing on the map is yours, and one node is you.

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #111 · AVERY'S LENS  The room has to hold without its most tired person  On the worst night, what saves the room is what was built on quiet days: a separate path, a written plan, words that belong to their owners — and a handover that lets the engineer go to sleep.  Every system in the room was under stress at once — including the engineer at hour fifteen.
Act III — “What the application stands on”

items.alt: The EOC in daylight the next morning; the wall shows a river gauge past its peak; Kit holds out a one-page brief; Maya, rested, takes it.

bubbles.text: Crested at 08:10. A record. Here's my brief — read it back to me.
Crest 08:10, carrier A's crew at ten, two items open…

items.caption: Handback is a handover too.

items.prompt: You could've stayed last night. Everyone would've understood.

options.label: “That's the problem. Everyone would've understood — right up to the wrong talkgroup.”
options.reply: Then I'll make sure nobody ever has to understand it. Go and write your application.

options.label: “The brief was good. You didn't need me.”
options.reply: That was the idea, wasn't it?

options.label: “I nearly did.”
options.reply: Nearly is what the roster's for.

items.prompt: 09:40. The state's rebuild grant closes at 08:00 tomorrow. What does the application stand on?
items.risk: An application the state can't tell from any other.
timeout: The application gets written at 04:00 from memory.

hints.text: What can you prove that nobody else applying can?

options.label: The design you've carried in your head since the after-action
options.result: A good design with nothing under it. The reviewers ask ‘why?’ eleven times.
options.consequence: An opinion, not a needs analysis.

options.label: The night as evidence: one timeline, what held and why, what nearly didn't — the shared conduit, the wall controller, the skipped generator test — each need traced to a finding, an owner and a number; then the design; then the five-year cost
options.result: By noon every need in the application points at a line in the night's timeline. Oduya: “Nobody can argue with last night.”
options.consequence: Needs from evidence, then design, then cost.

options.label: The biggest wall the grant will buy — reviewers like screens
options.result: Last night the wall froze and nobody noticed, because the handover wasn't on it.
options.consequence: Buys what's seen, not what's needed.

options.label: Ask for an extension — you've had a night
options.consequence: The deadline is the owner's, and it's fixed.

items.label: **Service Mode:** take the room back and build the evidence yourself.

items.alt: The EOC on Friday afternoon; Director Oduya holds Kit's one-page brief; Maya with the evidence pack for the application.

bubbles.text: He wrote ‘Nothing needed you. That was the point.’
Then the room worked. Now let's make the next one not need anyone to stay.

items.title: 09:00 · ‘two items open’
items.body: Kit's handback, one page: crest 08:10, a record; carrier A's crew at the cabinet at 10:00; the wall controller froze at 23:00 and Wendell restarted it at 23:04; two items open, each with an owner. At the bottom, in his writing: ‘Nothing needed you. That was the point.’

items.alt: The EOC the following week, quieter; Fitz with the patch-test sheet, Imogen with the template binder, Hektor with the generator log.

bubbles.text: Patch test Tuesday. Kit's running it.
Every warning went out word for word.
And the louvres are on the monthly test now.

items.alt: A design office at night, drawings pinned to every wall; Maya alone at a desk, a phone to her ear.

bubbles.text: We have sixty meeting rooms in thirty offices on four continents. They all work. Nobody can tell me why — and the people who know are retiring. Come and find out. Then leave it so it doesn't need you.

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  When everything is under stress at once: tell the director what can be trusted, including your own hours; use the separate path before the shared one fails (t = d ÷ v tells you when); relay warnings verbatim and answer rumours with the owner's facts in the PIO's words; leave power, networks, radios and evacuations to their owners; know your UPS minutes (t = E × η ÷ P); and hand the room over in writing — read, read back, signed — before the hour you know you make mistakes. The winning move on the worst night is often to go to sleep.
REFLECTION (optional)  · What in your work only holds because you stay late?
